title: How to set up events in Google Analytics 4
description: A practical GA4 event setup primer — enhanced measurement, custom events, key events (conversions), and common pitfalls — without dumping full vendor docs.
quickAnswer: In **GA4**, start with **enhanced measurement** for automatic pageviews/scrolls, then add **custom events** only for decisions you care about. Mark critical ones as **key events** (conversions). Prefer a short, named taxonomy over dozens of noisy tags.

sections.title: Start with enhanced measurement
sections.content:
After the GA4 tag is installed, turn on **enhanced measurement** for the basics (pageviews, outbound clicks, site search when configured). That covers many marketing sites without custom code.

Only add custom events when a dashboard or experiment depends on them — signup submit, pricing CTA, download, purchase.

sections.title: Custom events that stay useful
sections.content:
Use stable names (`signup_completed`, not `btn_click_hero_2`). Attach a few parameters (plan, location, value) — not twenty.

Send events via gtag, GTM, or your framework’s analytics helper. QA in DebugView before you trust reports.

sections.title: Mark conversions as key events
sections.content:
In GA4, mark the events that define success as **key events**. That powers conversion reporting and ads optimization when you link Google Ads.

If you do not run ads, you still want key events for cleaner exploration reports — just fewer of them.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
sections.content:
- Duplicate tags (GTM + hard-coded gtag) double-counting
- Consent mode misconfiguration changing event volume overnight
- Autocapture-style GTM clutter with no owners
- Comparing GA4 counts to Plausible pageviews as if they were the same metric

For when GA4 is overkill, read [GA4 vs Plausible](/compare/google-analytics-vs-plausible/). For product depth, see [GA4 vs PostHog](/compare/google-analytics-vs-posthog/).
